<thought>
REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 489 m apogee, and touches down under 3.2 m/s, with total flight time under 117.3 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
An ogive nose leads into a 67.1 mm body, and a conical transition steps down to a 50.3 mm aft tube. The narrow aft tube keeps total frontal area to 35.32 cm2, which limits drag. Four plywood trapezoid fins sit at the tail, far behind the center of gravity, so they supply most of the restoring force.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 0.526 kg, so the weight is 5.163 N. The G74W gives 85.29 N.s of impulse, or 162.0 N.s per kg. Thrust-to-weight is 14.8, well above 5:1, so the rocket leaves the 1.0 m rod at speed. The 29 mm motor fits its 48.26 mm mount with clearance.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 250.8 mm behind the CG, which gives a static margin of 3.741 calibers. That is well above the 1.0 caliber minimum. Because the margin is above about 3, the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more.

The 0.3048 m parachute opens at apogee. The 0.9144 m parachute opens at 200 m, so the landing speed is 3.189 m/s. That is 4.811 m/s under the 8 m/s limit, a wide margin.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 489.2 m with a peak speed of 141.2 m/s, Mach 0.416. Apogee comes at 9.15 s, and the full flight takes 117.3 s in 2 m/s wind.

The rocket has two stages and a 0.1005 m body diameter. A conical nose leads into the airframe, and three fin sets of four cardboard fins sit at the aft end. The largest set has a 0.1425 m root chord, which places fin area far behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 30.74 N at 3.134 kg. The design has a G80T at 133.2 N.s and an I300T at 436.7894 N.s, for a derived total of 570.0 N.s. That gives 181.9 N.s per kg. The thrust-to-weight ratio is not confirmed, so the rod exit speed cannot be stated from these facts.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 458.8 mm behind the CG, which is at 0.9634 m. Dividing by the 0.1005 m diameter gives a static margin of 4.565 calibers. That is well above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more.

Three parachutes deploy on ejection with a 200.0 m deploy altitude. The average sink rate over the 270 s descent is 5.21 m/s. The reference flight lands at 5.530 m/s, which is 2.470 m/s below the 8 m/s limit.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 1409 m with a peak speed of 172.6 m/s, Mach 0.51, and apogee at 17.03 s. The full flight takes 287.4 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The large impulse against 30.74 N of weight drives the high apogee.

- Flight time 300 s: the reference flight lasts 287.4 s.

AIRFRAME:
The ogive nose cone is 0.4254 m long and leads into a 101.6 mm body tube. The rocket is built from nine stages joined by couplers and centering rings, so it works as one long column of sections. The largest of the three fin sets spans 108 mm and sits far behind the center of gravity, which adds restoring force in the climb.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 51.0 N at 5.201 kg. The design has an AeroTech J315R with 757.2 N.s of total impulse and 296.9 N of average thrust, and an AeroTech J90W with 689.4 N.s. The 3.048 m launch rod keeps the rocket guided until it builds speed.

The CG is at 1.87 m and the CP is at 1.974 m, so the CP sits 103.4 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 1.018 calibers. That is just above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is stable with little room to spare. A small shift in mass or fin position would move the margin toward the limit.

Two parachutes are set. The 1.067 m chute deploys at 200 m altitude, and the 1.143 m chute deploys at apogee. The mean sink rate is 7.08 m/s over a 226.0 s descent. The reference landing speed is 5.554 m/s, which leaves 2.446 m/s below the 8 m/s limit.

The reference flight reaches 1602 m at a peak of 227.8 m/s, Mach 0.676. Apogee comes at 21.42 s, and the full flight takes 247.5 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The large total impulse explains the high apogee. The thin 1.018 caliber margin is the stability point to watch in this flight.

"Small one please, around 165 ft up. Keep it light, under 80 g, and it should come down slower than 5 m/s."

The rocket is a single-stage model with a 0.025 m diameter. A 0.1 m ogive nose leads into a 0.3 m body tube, and three small cardboard fins with 0.03 m spans sit at the tail. Their position far behind the center of gravity keeps the rocket pointed straight.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 0.6326 N at 0.06451 kg. The A8 motor is rated at 2.32 N.s with 3.475 N average thrust over 0.663 s. The thrust-to-weight ratio is 5.49, which is above the 5:1 guideline, so the rocket gains speed quickly off the 1.0 m rod.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 71.8 mm behind the CG, which is at 0.248 m. Dividing by the 0.025 m diameter gives a static margin of 2.872 calibers. That is well above the 1.0 caliber minimum but below 3, so the rocket is stable without being very stiff.

- Apogee request 165 ft: the reference flight reaches 50.55 m.
- Mass limit 80 g: liftoff mass is 0.06451 kg.

"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 2860 m apogee, and touches down under 7.8 m/s, with total flight time under 131.9 s, launched in about 4 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
The 46 mm airframe has a 0.18 m Haack nose cone and a tube with a 1.5 mm wall. Three aluminum fins, 2.5 mm thick, are set at the tail. Fins far behind the center of gravity give the restoring force that holds the rocket straight in the climb.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 15.15 N at 1.545 kg. The Cesaroni I216-CL(I) gives 636.1 N.s of total impulse and 217.0 N of average thrust over 2.924 s. Thrust-to-weight is 14.3, far above the 5:1 safety minimum, so the rocket leaves the 3.0 m rod with a strong push. The impulse is 411.8 N.s per kg, and that is the main energy input for the climb.

STABILITY:
The CG is at 0.598 m and the CP is at 0.682 m, so the CP sits 83.86 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 1.823 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum with room to spare, and the rocket is stable without being very stable.

A 0.61 m parachute deploys at 300 m altitude, and a streamer with a 0.5 m strip deploys on the ejection event. The mean sink rate is 25.7 m/s over the 111.0 s descent. That high average includes the fast early phase before the parachute opens. The reference landing speed is 7.721 m/s, which leaves only 0.2788 m/s below the 8 m/s limit. The landing is close to the limit and is not gentle.

The reference flight reaches 2862 m with a peak of 356.2 m/s, Mach 1.053, so it just passes Mach 1. Apogee comes at 20.62 s, and the full flight takes 131.8 s in 4.0 m/s wind. The landing at 7.721 m/s is the main concern, so the chute sizing needs review before the rocket is built.

REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 3740 m apogee, and touches down under 7.1 m/s, with total flight time under 151.1 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
A 0.18 m Haack nose cone leads into a 46 mm body. Trapezoid carbon fins with a 50 mm root chord and a 40 mm span sit at the tail. Their area lies far aft.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 1.882 kg, so the weight is 18.46 N. The J530 gives 1115 N.s of impulse, or 592.5 N.s per kg, with 547 N of average thrust over 2.037 s. Thrust-to-weight is 29.6, far above 5:1, so the rocket clears the rod very quickly. The 38 mm motor sits in a 38 mm mount with about zero clearance.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 69.98 mm behind the CG, which gives a static margin of 1.521 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum. The gap is short, so the margin stays modest, and wind has a larger effect than on a very stable rocket.

RECOVERY:
The 0.61 m parachute opens at 300 m, and a 0.5 m by 0.15 m streamer opens at 200 m. The landing speed is 7.001 m/s, which is 0.9994 m/s under the 8 m/s limit. This is near the limit, so the landing is firm, not gentle.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 3739 m with a peak of 559.2 m/s, Mach 1.653. Apogee comes at 21.23 s, and the flight lasts 151 s in 2 m/s wind. The coupler outer radius of 21.5 mm exceeds the 21.0 mm inner radius of the tube, a fit problem that must be fixed before building.

- Apogee request 3740 m: the reference flight reaches 3739 m.

- Flight time 151.1 s: the reference flight lasts 151 s.

REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 647 m apogee, and touches down under 5.3 m/s, with total flight time under 85.8 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
An ogive nose leads into an 80 mm body. Carbon fiber trapezoid fins with a 120 mm root chord and a 72 mm span sit at the tail. Their area lies far behind the center of gravity, which supplies the restoring force in the climb.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 4.789 kg, so the weight is 46.96 N. The I216 gives 636.1 N.s of impulse, or 132.8 N.s per kg, with 217 N of average thrust over 2.924 s. Thrust-to-weight is 4.62, below the 5:1 guide, so the rocket leaves the 1.0 m rod more slowly than a higher-ratio design. The 38 mm motor sits in a recorded 76 mm mount, which is twice the motor diameter.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 233.8 mm behind the CG, giving a static margin of 2.923 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum and above 2, so the rocket is stable without being extremely stiff.

RECOVERY:
The 1.595 m parachute opens at 300 m. The 0.3 m parachute opens at apogee after a 1.0 s delay. The landing speed is 5.255 m/s, which leaves 2.745 m/s under the 8 m/s limit, a comfortable margin.

The reference flight reaches 647 m with a peak of 104.5 m/s, Mach 0.308. Apogee comes at 12.35 s, and the flight lasts 85.71 s in 2 m/s wind. The 233.8 mm gap and 2.923 calibers keep the rocket stable through its climb.

REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 9680 m apogee, and touches down under 7.5 m/s, with total flight time under 443.2 s, launched in about 5.36 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
This two-stage design has a 57 mm airframe with a Haack nose cone and three fiberglass fins, each 3.175 mm thick. The fins have a 177.8 mm root chord and a 76.2 mm span, so they sit far behind the center of gravity and add a strong restoring force. The long body is built from several tube sections.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 79.93 N at 8.15 kg. The design has a Loki K627LR with 1526 N.s and a Cesaroni 3147L935-P with 3076 N.s. The derived total impulse is 4603 N.s, or 564.7 N.s per kg. Thrust-to-weight is not confirmed, so the rod exit cannot be rated from thrust. The 3.6576 m launch rod holds the rocket guided until it builds speed.

STABILITY:
The CG is at 1.949 m and the CP is at 2.515 m, so the CP sits 566.7 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 9.951 calibers. This is far above 3, so the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more. A margin this large can make the rocket weathercock into the wind.

RECOVERY:
Two large chutes, 1.067 m and 0.914 m, deploy at 304.8 m altitude. Two smaller chutes, 0.305 m and 0.457 m, deploy at apogee. The mean sink rate is 24.3 m/s over the 398.0 s descent. The reference landing speed is 7.454 m/s, which leaves 0.5463 m/s below the 8 m/s limit. That is close to the limit, so the landing is not gentle.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 9677 m with a peak of 515.1 m/s, Mach 1.588. Apogee comes at 45.1 s, and the full flight takes 443.2 s in 5.364 m/s wind. The high impulse drives this altitude. This is a fit problem: the K627LR motor is 38 mm, but the mount inner diameter is 37.1 mm, so the motor fit must be fixed before building.

REQUEST CHECK:
- Apogee request 9680 m: the reference flight reaches 9677 m.
- Touchdown limit 7.5 m/s: the reference flight lands at 7.454 m/s, within the limit.
- Flight time 443.2 s: the reference flight lasts 443.2 s.
- Wind 5.36 m/s: the reference flight used 5.364 m/s.

A 0.61 m Haack nose leads into a 102 mm body, built from two stages joined by tube couplers. Three carbon fiber trapezoid fins with a 200 mm root chord and a 100 mm tip chord sit at the tail.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 28.92 kg, so the weight is 283.6 N. Two motor entries are listed. The M1297W gives 5439 N.s with 1339 N of average thrust, and the N2000W gives 13260 N.s with 1927 N of average thrust. Together they total 18700 N.s, or 646.8 N.s per kg. Thrust-to-weight is not recorded, so rod exit speed is not confirmed. The M1297W fits its 76.2 mm mount with 1.2 mm clearance, but no mount check is recorded for the N2000W.

The CP sits 200.1 mm behind the CG, which gives a static margin of 1.962 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum, but well below 3, so the margin is adequate rather than large.

"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 105 m apogee, and touches down under 4.6 m/s, with total flight time under 30.5 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

The ogive nose cone is 65 mm long and leads into a 24.8 mm body. Two body tubes, 139 mm and 57 mm long, make the airframe, and a 70 mm inner tube holds the motor. Three PVC trapezoid fins have a 57 mm root chord, a 40 mm span, and a 0.1 mm thickness.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 45.78 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 24.8 mm diameter gives a static margin of 1.846 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is stable with some reserve.

The ogive nose cone is 340 mm long and has a 102 mm diameter at its aft end. Body tubes of 380 mm, 30 mm, 400 mm, and 740 mm make up the airframe, joined by tube couplers. The listed fin set is birch plywood, 3 mm thick.

The CP sits 256.8 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 102 mm diameter gives a static margin of 2.518 calibers. That is well above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is stable.

This two-stage design starts with a 343 mm ogive nose cone on a 67.1 mm body. A 79.25 mm conical transition steps the body up to a 79.4 mm section, so the upper airframe is wider. Liftoff mass is 3.411 kg, so the weight is 33.45 N. Two 38 mm motors are listed: the AeroTech HP-I280DM with 557.4 N.s and 283.0 N of average thrust, and the Loki J474-CT with 712.5 N.s and 470.2 N. The reference flight reaches 2396 m, with a peak of 380.1 m/s at Mach 1.128. Apogee comes at 18.7 s, and the flight lasts 124.3 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The ground hit is 7.283 m/s. The 2.391 caliber margin holds the supersonic climb steady, and the chute sizes set how close the landing comes to 8 m/s.

<thought>
REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 1610 m apogee, and touches down under 7.3 m/s, with total flight time under 130.6 s, launched in about 4.47 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
A 0.6096 m ogive nose leads into a 155.2 mm body, and a 0.9144 m aft section steps down to a 50 mm tube. Four freeform fiberglass fins, 6.35 mm thick, sit at the tail. Their area lies far behind the center of gravity, which supplies the restoring force.

The CP sits 327.5 mm behind the CG, giving a static margin of 2.11 calibers. That is above 1.0 but below 3, so the rocket is stable with a moderate margin.

<thought>
REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 380 m apogee, and touches down under 5 m/s, with total flight time under 99.8 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
The ellipsoid nose cone is 171 mm long and ends at a 41.6 mm aft diameter. A 457 mm body tube and a 216 mm body tube are joined by a 102 mm tube coupler. Three freeform balsa fins, 3.175 mm thick, are the only fin set listed.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 0.1771 kg, so the weight is 1.737 N. The Estes E9 gives 27.87 N.s of total impulse and 9.153 N of average thrust over a 3.042 s burn. Thrust-to-weight is 5.27, just above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 1.0 m rod with a modest margin. The 24 mm motor fits the 24.13 mm mount with 0.13 mm of clearance. Impulse per kilogram is 157.4 N.s/kg.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 191.2 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 41.58 mm diameter gives a static margin of 4.597 calibers. This is above 3, so the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more.

RECOVERY:
A 0.4572 m parachute deploys at ejection. The reference landing speed is 4.568 m/s, which is 3.432 m/s under the 8 m/s limit, a wide margin. The mean sink rate is 4.17 m/s over a 91.0 s descent.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 379.7 m, with a peak of 97.94 m/s at Mach 0.2891. Apogee comes at 8.711 s, and the flight lasts 99.76 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The ground hit is 4.568 m/s. This is a fit problem: the nose cone aft shoulder radius of 20.26 mm exceeds the adjacent tube inner radius of 20.23 mm, so the nose cone does not fit and must be fixed before building.

- Flight time 99.8 s: the reference flight lasts 99.76 s.
- Wind 2 m/s: the reference flight used 2 m/s.
</thought>

An ogive nose leads into a 140 mm body, with 0.505 m, 0.605 m, and 1.065 m body sections and an 80 mm inner tube. The fin layout is unusual: one set has two 50 mm root-chord cardboard fins, and another set has a single 495 mm root-chord fin. A single fin gives unbalanced side force.

The CP sits 178.2 mm behind the CG, giving a static margin of 1.273 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum, but the margin is modest for a rocket this large.

A 1.524 m parachute opens at 250 m, and a 0.6096 m parachute opens at apogee. The landing speed is 7.224 m/s, which leaves 0.776 m/s under the 8 m/s limit. This is near the limit, so the landing is firm.

The reference flight reaches 2462 m with a peak of 240.7 m/s, Mach 0.715. Apogee comes at 22.43 s, and the flight lasts 170.1 s in 2 m/s wind. The asymmetric fin layout and the 1.273 calibers margin are the main stability points to check before building.

- Apogee request 8,080 ft: the reference flight reaches 2462 m.
- Touchdown limit 7.3 m/s: the reference flight lands at 7.224 m/s, within the limit.
- Diameter limit 160 mm: the body is 140 mm.

The 102 mm airframe has a 0.5 m Haack nose cone on a 1.9 m body built from several tube sections. Four fiberglass fins, 6 mm thick, have a 300 mm root chord, a 75 mm tip chord, and a 110 mm span. Those large fins add restoring force behind the center of gravity.

The 98 mm motor fills its 98 mm mount with about zero clearance.

The CG is at 1.758 m and the CP is at 2.138 m, so the CP sits 380.0 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 3.725 calibers. That is above 3, so the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more.

"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 1000 m apogee, and touches down under 6.9 m/s, with total flight time under 159.1 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

The rocket is a single stage with a 0.054 m diameter and a 0.05 m ogive nose. A single 0.82 m body tube forms most of the airframe and carries a 0.111 kg altimeter. Three fiberglass fins with 0.07 m root chords and 0.055 m spans sit at the tail, with a 0.09925 m sweep that sets their trailing edges well back.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 6.885 N at 0.7021 kg. The design has one H283ST rated at 199.1 N.s with 269.7 N average thrust over 0.7382 s, and a 7.0 s ejection delay. The derived impulse is 283.5 N.s per kg. The thrust-to-weight ratio is 39.2, far above the 5:1 guideline, so the rocket leaves the 1.0 m rod very quickly. The motor fits the mount with 0.014 m clearance.

The CP sits 89.47 mm behind the CG, which is at 0.546 m. Dividing by the 0.054 m diameter gives a static margin of 1.657 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum but below 3, so the rocket is stable without being very stiff.

The ogive nose cone is 324 mm long and has a 101.6 mm diameter at its aft end. A 279 mm body tube and an 864 mm body tube are joined by a 152 mm tube coupler. Three freeform aircraft plywood fins, 3.175 mm thick, are the only fin set listed.

Liftoff mass is 1.712 kg, so the weight is 16.79 N. The AeroTech HP-H135W gives 229.0 N.s of total impulse and 115.9 N of average thrust over a 1.973 s burn. The CP sits 200.2 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 101.6 mm diameter gives a static margin of 1.97 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is stable with a moderate reserve.

Liftoff mass is 7.0 kg, so the weight is 68.65 N. The Cesaroni K660 gives 2437 N.s of total impulse and 681.3 N of average thrust over a 3.573 s burn. AIRFRAME:
The 150 mm airframe has a 0.43 m Haack nose cone and carries a 2.0 kg payload. Three carbon fiber fins, 5 mm thick, sit at the tail with a 280 mm root chord and a 142 mm span. Their 229.4 mm sweep puts the fin tips far aft, which keeps the fin area behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 335.3 N at 34.2 kg. The Cesaroni 11077N2600-P gives 11070 N.s of total impulse and 2599 N of average thrust over 4.26 s. STABILITY:
The CG is at 1.858 m and the CP is at 2.043 m, so the CP sits 184.7 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 1.232 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum by a modest amount, so the rocket is stable without being very stable.

AIRFRAME:
The 150 mm airframe has a 0.43 m Haack nose cone and carries a 2.0 kg payload. Three carbon fiber fins, 5 mm thick, sit at the tail with a 280 mm root chord and a 142 mm span. Their 229.4 mm sweep puts the fin tips far aft, which keeps the fin area behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 335.3 N at 34.2 kg. The Cesaroni 11077N2600-P gives 11070 N.s of total impulse and 2599 N of average thrust over 4.26 s. The CG is at 1.858 m and the CP is at 2.043 m, so the CP sits 184.7 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 1.232 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum by a modest amount, so the rocket is stable without being very stable.

The 79.4 mm airframe has a 0.3366 m ogive nose cone and two body tube sections of 0.3048 m and 0.9144 m. Two sets of four G10 phenolic fins, each 1.6 mm thick, sit at the tail. The first set has an 85.7 mm root chord that tapers to a near-zero tip, with a 50.8 mm span. The second has a 133.3 mm root chord, a 38.1 mm tip chord, and a 98.4 mm span.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 17.03 N at 1.736 kg. The AeroTech HP-H182R gives 216.1 N.s of total impulse and 177.1 N of average thrust over 1.22 s. Thrust-to-weight is 10.4, far above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 1.5 m rod quickly. The impulse is 124.5 N.s per kg. The 29 mm motor fits a 29.08 mm mount with 0.083 mm clearance.

The CG is at 1.016 m and the CP is at 1.219 m, so the CP sits 203.8 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 2.566 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum with room, and it is below 3, so the rocket is stable without being very stable.

The reference flight reaches 473.1 m with a peak of 111.4 m/s, Mach 0.3278. Apogee comes at 9.735 s, and the full flight takes 74.71 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The 10.4 thrust-to-weight gives a fast climb, and the 7.526 m/s landing is the main point to check.

"Get it to about 3,160 ft, with touchdown at 8 m/s or less, flight close to 2.5 minutes. Body 3.5 inches wide at most and under 2.2 kg."

AIRFRAME:
The ogive nose cone is 337 mm long and sits on a 79.4 mm body with a 914 mm main tube. Four G10 phenolic trapezoid fins are listed in two sets, both 1.6 mm thick. The larger set has a 133.3 mm root chord and a 98.4 mm span, which adds fin area behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 2.127 kg, so the weight is 20.86 N. The AeroTech I305FJ gives 443.9 N.s of total impulse and 293.2 N of average thrust over a 1.511 s burn. Thrust-to-weight is 14.1, so the rocket leaves the 2.0 m rod with strong acceleration. The 38 mm motor fits its 38.7 mm mount with 0.735 mm of clearance, and its 288 mm length fits the 368 mm mount. Impulse per kilogram is 208.7 N.s/kg.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 131.4 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 79.4 mm diameter gives a static margin of 1.655 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum, so the rocket is stable with a moderate reserve.

RECOVERY:
A 0.9144 m parachute with a drag coefficient of 0.75 deploys at ejection. The reference landing speed is 7.96 m/s, only 0.0405 m/s under the 8 m/s limit. That is essentially at the limit, so the landing is not gentle. This single chute is the only recovery element listed.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 963.3 m, with a peak of 187.4 m/s and a rail exit speed of 26.56 m/s. The flight lasts 135.6 s, and the ground hit is 7.96 m/s. The 14.1 thrust-to-weight gives the fast rail exit, and the 1.655 caliber margin keeps the rocket stable. Mach number and wind are not recorded for this reference flight.

REQUEST CHECK:
- Apogee request 3,160 ft: the reference flight reaches 963.3 m.
- Touchdown limit 8 m/s: the reference flight lands at 7.96 m/s, within the limit.
- Flight time 2.5 minutes: the reference flight lasts 135.6 s.
- Diameter limit 3.5 inches: the body is 79.4 mm.

"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 1680 m apogee, and touches down under 6.7 m/s, with total flight time under 272.2 s, launched in about 2 m/s wind. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
The 102.2 mm airframe has a 0.4254 m ogive nose cone and a 0.7239 m body tube. Two fin sets of G10 phenolic sit at the tail. One has a 152.4 mm root chord that tapers to a near-zero tip, and the other has a 177.8 mm root chord, a 50.8 mm tip chord, and a 139.7 mm span. Both sets are 1.6 mm thick, and their position far aft adds restoring force behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 43.8 N at 4.467 kg. The AeroTech HP-K535W gives 1429.0 N.s of total impulse and 509.5 N of average thrust over 2.801 s. Thrust-to-weight is 11.6, far above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 3.0 m rod with a strong push. The impulse is 319.8 N.s per kg. The 54 mm motor fits a 54.66 mm mount with 0.66 mm clearance.

STABILITY:
The CG is at 1.327 m and the CP is at 1.537 m, so the CP sits 209.8 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 2.053 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum with clear room, and it is below 3, so the rocket is stable without being very stable.

Two parachutes deploy on the ejection event. A 1.524 m parachute and a 0.4572 m parachute, both with a drag coefficient of 0.75, open at ejection. The mean sink rate is 6.56 m/s over the 256.0 s descent. The reference landing speed is 6.632 m/s, which leaves 1.368 m/s below the 8 m/s limit.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 1677 m with a peak of 260.4 m/s, Mach 0.7688. Apogee comes at 16.6 s, and the full flight takes 272.1 s in 2.0 m/s wind. The 11.6 thrust-to-weight and the 1429.0 N.s impulse drive the climb, and the 1.368 m/s landing margin is the chute result to note.

- Flight time 272.2 s: the reference flight lasts 272.1 s.

Two sets of four G10 phenolic trapezoid fins are listed, both 1.6 mm thick. The larger set has a 177.8 mm root chord and a 120.7 mm span.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 2.64 kg, so the weight is 25.89 N. The AeroTech H268R gives 309.5 N.s of total impulse and 267.3 N of average thrust over a 1.156 s burn. STABILITY:
The CP sits 244.6 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 102.2 mm diameter gives a static margin of 2.393 calibers. That is above the 1.0 caliber minimum and below 3, so the rocket is stable with a moderate reserve.

A 1.3716 m parachute with a drag coefficient of 0.75 deploys at ejection. The reference landing speed is 6.307 m/s, which is 1.693 m/s under the 8 m/s limit. The large chute is the only recovery element listed, and it sets the descent speed.

The reference flight reaches 433.0 m, with a peak of 104.4 m/s and a rail exit speed of 18.24 m/s. The flight lasts 81.66 s, and the ground hit is 6.307 m/s. The 10.3 thrust-to-weight gives the quick rail exit, and the 2.393 caliber margin keeps the rocket stable. Apogee time and wind are not recorded for this flight.

PROPULSION:

AIRFRAME:\nThe 58.4 mm airframe has a 0.2413 m ogive nose cone and two body sections of 0.5461 m and 0.7493 m, joined by a short 0.0254 m transition. Two fin sets are listed: four trapezoid fins 1.587 mm thick with a 38.1 mm root chord and a 19.1 mm span, and four freeform fins 1.6 mm thick. Those fins add restoring force behind the center of gravity.\n\nPROPULSION:\nLiftoff weight is 12.88 N at 1.314 kg. The AeroTech H238T gives 177.6 N.s of total impulse and 188.7 N of average thrust over 0.9383 s. Thrust-to-weight is 14.7, far above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 2.0 m rod quickly. The static margin is 3.17 calibers. That is above 3, so the rocket is very stable and may turn into the wind more.\n\nRECOVERY:
\nA 0.762 m parachute with a drag coefficient of 0.75 deploys on the ejection event. The mean sink rate is 7.64 m/s over the 74.8 s descent. The reference landing speed is 7.851 m/s, which leaves only 0.149 m/s below the 8 m/s limit. That is very close to the limit, so the landing is not gentle.\n\n

The 14.7 thrust-to-weight drives a fast climb, and the 7.851 m/s landing is the main point to check. "I'd like it at about 1,880 ft with a touchdown of 7.9 m/s or less. Diameter near 2.4 inches, around 1.5 kg, flight close to 90 seconds."

Two fin sets are listed: four trapezoid fins 1.587 mm thick with a 38.1 mm root chord and a 19.1 mm span, and four freeform fins 1.6 mm thick. Those fins add restoring force behind the center of gravity.\n\nPROPULSION:\nLiftoff weight is 12.88 N at 1.314 kg. The AeroTech H238T gives 177.6 N.s of total impulse and 188.7 N of average thrust over 0.9383 s. Thrust-to-weight is 14.7, far above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 2.0 m rod quickly. Six trapezoid balsa fins have a 0.1333 m root chord, a near-zero tip chord, and a 0.05715 m span. The fins are 0.003175 m thick, which is thicker than the glass fins elsewhere in this set.

PROPULSION:
The motor is a Cesaroni 116G126-13A, rated at 115.63 N.s total impulse with 125.5 N average thrust over a 0.9205 s burn. The ejection delay is 8.0 s. The center of gravity sits at 0.7551 m and the center of pressure at 0.9347 m, so the CP sits 179.7 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 3.076 calibers. AIRFRAME:
The 58.4 mm airframe has a 0.2413 m ogive nose cone on body tubes of 0.3048 m and 0.6096 m. Six balsa trapezoid fins, 3.175 mm thick, have a 133.3 mm root chord and a 57.2 mm span, with a near-zero tip. Those fins sit at the tail and add restoring force behind the center of gravity.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff weight is 12.2 N at 1.244 kg. The AeroTech H73J gives 188.3 N.s of total impulse and 70.0 N of average thrust over 2.682 s. Thrust-to-weight is 5.74, just above the 5:1 minimum, so the rocket leaves the 2.5 m rod with a modest push. The impulse is 151.3 N.s per kg. The 38 mm motor fits a 38.73 mm mount with 0.735 mm clearance.

STABILITY:
The CG is at 0.774 m and the CP is at 0.935 m, so the CP sits 161.0 mm behind the CG. The static margin is 2.756 calibers. That clears the 1.0 caliber minimum with room, and it is below 3, so the rocket is stable without being very stable.

A 0.762 m parachute with a drag coefficient of 0.75 deploys on the ejection event. The mean sink rate is 7.24 m/s over the 96.4 s descent. The reference landing speed is 7.433 m/s, which leaves 0.567 m/s below the 8 m/s limit. That is close to the limit, so the landing is not gentle.

Two fin sets of G10 fiberglass sit at the tail: four freeform fins, 1.6 mm thick, and four trapezoid fins with a 177.8 mm root chord, a 50.8 mm tip chord, and a 127 mm span. Both sets add restoring force behind the center of gravity.

The design has an AeroTech I65W with 630.5 N.s and 88.3 N of average thrust over 7.095 s, and a Loki J350-SF with 986.5 N.s and 378.3 N of average thrust over 2.605 s. The derived total impulse is 1617 N.s, or 305.3 N.s per kg. Thrust-to-weight is not confirmed, so the rod exit is not rated. The 3.0 m launch rod is the length the rocket must clear. <thought>
REQUEST:
"Design a complete model rocket that reaches about 508 m apogee, and touches down under 6.1 m/s, with total flight time under 99.7 s. Provide the complete hardware design."

AIRFRAME:
The ogive nose cone is 337 mm long and ends at a 78.7 mm diameter. Body tubes of 483 mm, 432 mm, and 356 mm, at a 79.4 mm diameter, make the main airframe. A 44.5 mm conical transition steps down to a smaller section. Three G10 phenolic trapezoid fins are 1.6 mm thick, with a 215.9 mm root chord, a 108 mm span, and an 184.1 mm sweep.

PROPULSION:
Liftoff mass is 2.17 kg, so the weight is 21.28 N. The Cesaroni 269H110-14A gives 270.6 N.s of total impulse and 106.4 N of average thrust over a 2.54 s burn. Thrust-to-weight is 5.0, so the rocket leaves the 2.0 m rod at the 5:1 level. The 38 mm motor fits its 38.73 mm mount with 0.735 mm of clearance, and its 186 mm length fits the 368 mm mount. Impulse per kilogram is 124.7 N.s/kg.

STABILITY:
The CP sits 186.3 mm behind the CG. Dividing by the 79.4 mm diameter gives a static margin of 2.347 calibers. That is above 1.0 and below 3, so the rocket is stable with a moderate reserve.

RECOVERY:
Two chutes are listed, and both deploy on the same ejection event at 200 m altitude. A 1.22 m chute has a drag coefficient of 0.75 and a 0.1247 kg mass, and a 0.457 m chute has the same drag coefficient. The reference landing speed is 6.025 m/s, which is 1.975 m/s under the 8 m/s limit. Because the larger chute carries most of the drag, it sets the landing speed.

FLIGHT CHECK:
The reference flight reaches 508.2 m, with a peak of 98.78 m/s and a rail exit speed of 12.99 m/s. The flight lasts 99.67 s, and the ground hit is 6.025 m/s. The 5.0 thrust-to-weight gives a moderate start, and the 2.347 caliber margin keeps the rocket stable.

REQUEST CHECK:
- Apogee request 508 m: the reference flight reaches 508.2 m.
- Touchdown limit 6.1 m/s: the reference flight lands at 6.025 m/s, within the limit.
- Flight time 99.7 s: the reference flight lasts 99.67 s.
</thought>
